text.p: Nigeria's military government has abolished fertiliser subsidies in favour of a new plan to provide soft and short term loans to farmers, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.

"The federal government has totally removed the subsidy on fertiliser because of the large scale corruption that characterised its procurement and distribution over the years," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters in the capital Abuja.

"What it means is that the federal government is no longer involved in procurement and distribution of fertilisers. Farmers can now source for fertiliser in the open market or anywhere and be ready to pay the price they are offered," he added.
Procuring fertiliser has been a major problem for Nigerian farmers, who last month warned of the prospects of poor harvests this year because of their inability to obtain the commodity.
They said farmers had resorted to using organic manure, which was not good enough.
A 50kg bag of fertiliser, which used to cost the subsidised price of 150 naira ($1.77), now sells at 1,500 naira ($17.7).
The fertiliser debacle caused military ruler General Sani Abacha to meet in mid-June in Abuja with state military administrators but no statement was issued after the talks.
The agriculture ministry official said it had been decided that individuals and businesses could now either import fertiliser to sell to farmers or set up feriliser plants in the country.
"The government has now deregulated the production, procurement and distribution of the product," he said.
Cheap loans with minimal or no collataral will be available to farmers, he said, adding "the subsidies that has been removed will be channelled into soft and short term loans to farmers."
A spokesman for the National Fertiliser Company (NAFCON) said recently that the company had received a directive from the government to fully commercialise its operations.
In compliance with the directive the company recently advertised for distributors and marketers, he said.
"The good thing in this is that fertiliser will from now be easily available as there will be no more hoarding," said the agriculture ministry official.
